chunks: Yahya ibn Abi al-ʿAlaʾ narrated from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said:
"A fasting person in the Month of Ramadan while traveling is like one who breaks his fast in it while resident."

Then he said: "A man came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, should I fast the Month of Ramadan while traveling?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, it is easy for me.' So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has bestowed charity upon the sick of my community and its travelers through breaking the fast in the Month of Ramadan. Would any one of you love, when he gives a charity, that it be returned to him?'"

key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: residence, being at home and not traveling
key_terms.بِالْإِفْطَارِ: by breaking the fast, the granted allowance not to fast
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan, the obligatory month of sawm
key_terms.مَرْضَى: the sick, those affected by illness
key_terms.مُسَافِرِيهَا: its travelers, members of the community who are journeying

ai.seo_question: Can a traveler fast in Ramadan if fasting is easy for him?
ai.summary: This hadith states that fasting during travel in the Month of Ramadan is not the prescribed ruling, and it likens it to breaking the fast while resident. It further explains through the words of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم that الإفطار for the sick and travelers is a divine concession and gift that should be accepted, not refused.
